credit.instrument: Bank facilities - LT Rs404.55cr; LT/ST Rs225cr; ST Rs40cr
credit.prior_rating: CARE BBB+; Stable / CARE A3+ (reaffirmed; LT amount enhanced from Rs188.64cr)
credit.rationale: Reaffirmed. Ratings derive strength from DCIL's nearly five-decade presence in domestic and overseas dredging, strong parentage (shareholding held by major ports; promoter unsecured loans of Rs342 cr as on 28-Feb-2026), and a growing order book (Rs1,422 cr as on 30-Sep-2025, ~1.25 years' revenue visibility). Rating strengths are tempered by an ageing dredger fleet (avg age >23 years) with high maintenance expense, unhedged foreign-exchange risk (Rs36 cr forex loss in 9MFY26; forex loan hedged since Dec 2025), fuel-price volatility, and competition from foreign players. FY25 net loss (PAT -Rs27 cr) hit by Rs118 cr liquidated damages; PBILDT margin 12.23% (FY25) improving to 14.35% (9MFY26) on Rs17 cr LD recovery. Commissioning of India's largest dredger DCI Dredge Godavari (scheduled ~Oct 2026) to enable capital dredging and improve scale/debt-coverage from FY27. Overall gearing 0.95x (FY25), below unity.

bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Support from promoter ports; Commissioning of new dredger
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- scale: undertakes nearly 80% of India's maintenance dredging operations — evidence: "we undertake nearly 80% of India's maintenance dredging operations"
- customer lock-in: promoted and anchored by four major port authorities that are also its principal customers — evidence: "DCI is promoted by four major port authorities, providing stable access to maintenance, dredging contracts and improving long-term business visibility"
- scale: operates one of the country's largest dredging fleets (10 TSHDs, 1 CSD, 1 Backhoe Dredger, 1 Inland Cutter Suction Dredger plus ancillary craft) — evidence: "The Company operates one of the country's largest dredging fleets, supporting maintenance dredging, reclamation, beach nourishment and coastal infrastructure projects"
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Foreign exchange risk — Import-dependent procurement, vessel-related expenses, foreign currency debt servicing and overseas operations expose the Company to adverse currency movements affecting project costs, profitability and cash flows.
- Ageing dredger fleet / financial risk — An ageing fleet (>25 years for some vessels) leads to frequent breakdowns and emergency dry-docking; maintenance delays caused by liquidity limitations lead to penalties and project delays, compounded by elevated debt levels and higher interest outflows.
- Human capital risk — Availability and retention of skilled marine personnel, dredging specialists and technical workforce is important for uninterrupted project execution and fleet operations.
- Cybersecurity risk — Increasing digital integration across vessel operations and monitoring systems has heightened exposure to cyber threats, system disruptions and data security risks.
- Natural disasters and climate risk — Extreme weather events, cyclones and rough sea conditions may impact dredging schedules, vessel deployment and coastal infrastructure operations, increasing risk of operational disruption and infrastructure damage.
- Legal and compliance risk — Operations are subject to maritime regulations, environmental norms, port authority requirements and contractual compliance obligations; non-adherence risks legal penalties, operational disruption and reputational impact.
- Market competition risk — Competition from domestic and international dredging companies may impact pricing, project margins and order inflows across key maritime segments.
- Business/customer concentration risk — A significant portion of the Company's business is linked to projects awarded by port authorities and government maritime infrastructure programmes, including its own promoter ports, concentrating demand in government-led infrastructure.

outlook.body: Commissioning of new dredger, DCI Dredge Godavari, expected to enhance capacity and support growth
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Fleet modernisation through the planned induction of 11 modern dredgers over the next five years, announced during India Maritime Week 2025
- Building future dredgers domestically (Make in India / Atmanirbhar Bharat), including the DCI Dredge Godavari at Cochin Shipyard with technical collaboration from Royal IHC of the Netherlands
- Strengthening long-term business visibility through MoUs signed with major ports and maritime organisations during FY 2025-26
- Examining longer-duration (5-10 year) dredging contracts, in line with the Ministry's direction, to align capacity planning, business visibility and asset investment
- Increasing participation in capital dredging, reclamation, inland waterways and coastal infrastructure development projects across Indian ports
- Expanding international presence through joint ventures with global players and chartering arrangements
- Exploring dry-docking and ship-repair facilities with shipyards and greenfield ports to reduce turnaround time, including discussions with Hindustan Shipyard Limited and Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited
- Assessing opportunities in inland waterways, reservoir and dam desiltation, marine construction, offshore installations and subsea cable trenching
- Integrating e-governance and digital technologies (monitoring systems, RFID inventory, ICC/PMS/SCAD upgradation) across operations to improve efficiency
- Promoting training and recruitment activities to strengthen workforce capabilities for new-generation vessels and business areas
- Disciplined capital allocation to match fleet expansion with visibility of work and sound utilisation
outlook.title: Strategy

outlook.body: DCI has initiated a major fleet modernisation programme to procure 11 new dredgers (higher-capacity TSHDs, CSDs, Inland Cutter Dredgers of 350-650 m3, and a Water Injection Dredger) over the next five years. The first new-build, the 12,000 m3 TSHD 'DCI Dredge Godavari', is under construction at Cochin Shipyard Limited under the Atmanirbhar Bharat / Make in India initiative, with technical collaboration from Royal IHC of the Netherlands; it was launched on 18 October 2025 and its commissioning is expected in late 2026 / delivery protocols by October 2026, joining the fleet in FY2026-27. A second 12,000 m3 TSHD is in the process of being ordered, targeted for FY2026-27. The Company is also exploring dry-docking and ship-repair facility collaborations with Hindustan Shipyard Limited and Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited to reduce turnaround time for its existing fleet.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's maritime sector is entering a period of transformation, with growing port capacity, deeper navigation channels, rising cargo volumes and greater emphasis on inland waterways, expected to demand larger and more specialised dredging capability
- Rising cargo volumes and deployment of larger vessels are driving demand for deeper navigational channels at Indian ports
- Government focus on inland water transport and fairway development is expected to create additional opportunities for channel maintenance and navigational dredging
- Coastal economic zones, port-linked industrial development and waterfront infrastructure projects may increase demand for dredging and reclamation activities
- Offshore wind projects and subsea infrastructure development could create demand for specialised marine and seabed preparation services
- Climate-related coastal erosion and shoreline protection initiatives are expected to support demand for beach nourishment activities
- Ageing fleet profile requiring periodic refurbishment and dry-docking is a constraint on capacity utilisation and availability
- MoUs signed at India Maritime Week 2025 (aggregate value ~INR17,645 crore, 16 organisations) improved order-book visibility and revenue stability
- 22 MoUs signed during India Maritime Week 2025 with 16 organisations, aggregate value approximately INR17,645 crore, spanning two to five years
- Major port agreements with Mumbai Port Authority (Maintenance and Capital Dredging, INR510 crore, 2-5 years, including a specific INR60 crore allocation for capital dredging), Visakhapatnam Port (comprehensive dredging services, 3-5 years), Paradip Port Authority (deepening and fairway maintenance, 2-5 years), Jawaharlal Nehru Port (channel and basin maintenance, 2-5 years) and Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port (continued maintenance in the Hooghly Estuary, 5 years)
- Five-year maintenance dredging contract for Mumbai Harbour and JN Port channels
- First year completed of a three-year contract to develop and maintain a 32-metre fairway in the North Eastern Region

The programme to acquire 11 new dredgers over the next five years represents an indicative investment of ₹3,560 crore, to be funded through a combination of equity and debt.
DCI is deliberating a rights issue of approximately ₹1,000 crore to support capacity expansion and the acquisition of high-capacity vessels.

The Company cites a projected total dredging capacity of 80 million m3 and deep-water dredging capability of 36 metres associated with its fleet modernisation.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: India's leading dredging and allied marine services provider, undertaking nearly 80% of the country's maintenance dredging operations.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Dredging Corporation of India Limited provides integrated dredging and allied marine services — maintenance dredging, capital dredging, land reclamation, beach nourishment, inland and shallow water dredging, and project management consultancy — to major and non-major ports, the Indian Navy, shipyards, fishing harbours and other maritime organisations. It also undertakes marine construction support and hydrographic/bathymetric survey services.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Visakhapatnam Port Authority — related party: Principal promoter/port authority; significant influence; dredging contract counterparty
- Paradip Port Authority — related party: Principal promoter/port authority; significant influence; dredging contract counterparty
- Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority — related party: Principal promoter/port authority; significant influence; dredging contract counterparty
- Deendayal Port Authority — related party: Principal promoter/port authority; significant influence; dredging contract counterparty

products.body: - **Dredging & Allied Marine Services:** Maintenance dredging, Capital dredging, Land reclamation, Beach nourishment, Inland / shallow water dredging, Project management consultancy, Marine construction support, Hydrographic and survey services

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's maritime sector is entering a period of transformation, with growing port capacity, deeper navigation channels, rising cargo volumes and greater emphasis on inland waterways, expected to demand larger and more specialised dredging capability
- Rising cargo volumes and deployment of larger vessels are driving demand for deeper navigational channels at Indian ports
- Government focus on inland water transport and fairway development is expected to create additional opportunities for channel maintenance and navigational dredging
- Coastal economic zones, port-linked industrial development and waterfront infrastructure projects may increase demand for dredging and reclamation activities
- Offshore wind projects and subsea infrastructure development could create demand for specialised marine and seabed preparation services
- Climate-related coastal erosion and shoreline protection initiatives are expected to support demand for beach nourishment activities
- Ageing fleet profile requiring periodic refurbishment and dry-docking is a constraint on capacity utilisation and availability
- MoUs signed at India Maritime Week 2025 (aggregate value ~INR17,645 crore, 16 organisations) improved order-book visibility and revenue stability
- 22 MoUs signed during India Maritime Week 2025 with 16 organisations, aggregate value approximately INR17,645 crore, spanning two to five years
- Major port agreements with Mumbai Port Authority (Maintenance and Capital Dredging, INR510 crore, 2-5 years, including a specific INR60 crore allocation for capital dredging), Visakhapatnam Port (comprehensive dredging services, 3-5 years), Paradip Port Authority (deepening and fairway maintenance, 2-5 years), Jawaharlal Nehru Port (channel and basin maintenance, 2-5 years) and Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port (continued maintenance in the Hooghly Estuary, 5 years)
- Five-year maintenance dredging contract for Mumbai Harbour and JN Port channels
- First year completed of a three-year contract to develop and maintain a 32-metre fairway in the North Eastern Region

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: PBILDT Margin: 12.23% (FY25); Fuel costs: high due to geopolitical developments

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Promoter support: 342 crore of unsecured loans; Debt financing: 400 crore term loan

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: DCI has initiated a major fleet modernisation programme to procure 11 new dredgers (higher-capacity TSHDs, CSDs, Inland Cutter Dredgers of 350-650 m3, and a Water Injection Dredger) over the next five years. The first new-build, the 12,000 m3 TSHD 'DCI Dredge Godavari', is under construction at Cochin Shipyard Limited under the Atmanirbhar Bharat / Make in India initiative, with technical collaboration from Royal IHC of the Netherlands; it was launched on 18 October 2025 and its commissioning is expected in late 2026 / delivery protocols by October 2026, joining the fleet in FY2026-27. A second 12,000 m3 TSHD is in the process of being ordered, targeted for FY2026-27. The Company is also exploring dry-docking and ship-repair facility collaborations with Hindustan Shipyard Limited and Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited to reduce turnaround time for its existing fleet.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- scale: undertakes nearly 80% of India's maintenance dredging operations — evidence: "we undertake nearly 80% of India's maintenance dredging operations"
- customer lock-in: promoted and anchored by four major port authorities that are also its principal customers — evidence: "DCI is promoted by four major port authorities, providing stable access to maintenance, dredging contracts and improving long-term business visibility"
- scale: operates one of the country's largest dredging fleets (10 TSHDs, 1 CSD, 1 Backhoe Dredger, 1 Inland Cutter Suction Dredger plus ancillary craft) — evidence: "The Company operates one of the country's largest dredging fleets, supporting maintenance dredging, reclamation, beach nourishment and coastal infrastructure projects"

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Ageing fleet; Foreign exchange risk; Competition from foreign players

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Support from promoter ports; Commissioning of new dredger

strategy.title: Strategy
strategy.body:
- Fleet modernisation through the planned induction of 11 modern dredgers over the next five years, announced during India Maritime Week 2025
- Building future dredgers domestically (Make in India / Atmanirbhar Bharat), including the DCI Dredge Godavari at Cochin Shipyard with technical collaboration from Royal IHC of the Netherlands
- Strengthening long-term business visibility through MoUs signed with major ports and maritime organisations during FY 2025-26
- Examining longer-duration (5-10 year) dredging contracts, in line with the Ministry's direction, to align capacity planning, business visibility and asset investment
- Increasing participation in capital dredging, reclamation, inland waterways and coastal infrastructure development projects across Indian ports
- Expanding international presence through joint ventures with global players and chartering arrangements
- Exploring dry-docking and ship-repair facilities with shipyards and greenfield ports to reduce turnaround time, including discussions with Hindustan Shipyard Limited and Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited
- Assessing opportunities in inland waterways, reservoir and dam desiltation, marine construction, offshore installations and subsea cable trenching
- Integrating e-governance and digital technologies (monitoring systems, RFID inventory, ICC/PMS/SCAD upgradation) across operations to improve efficiency
- Promoting training and recruitment activities to strengthen workforce capabilities for new-generation vessels and business areas
- Disciplined capital allocation to match fleet expansion with visibility of work and sound utilisation

themes.title: Naval shipbuilding & maritime
themes.need: A multi-decade naval order book and indigenous warship/submarine build, plus the naval-equipment supply chain (HVAC/chillers, mechanical seals, marine gearing) and maritime services, underpin the theme. GRSE carries a large RFP pipeline (~INR1.5 lakh cr referenced); SHREE REFRIGERATIONS 544458 supplies naval HVAC; SEALMATIC 543782 naval/submarine seals; ELECON defence-marine gearing; KMEW/SEAMECLTD/DREDGECORP maritime services.
themes.driver: Fresh MoD warship/submarine orders + naval-equipment indigenization inflow; maritime-infra/offshore contract wins.

themes.title: Maritime shipping & terminalling
themes.need: Shipping and liquid/gas terminalling players are driven by freight/charter cycles, terminalling tariffs and energy-cargo throughput - not the e-comm/quick-comm/GST-warehousing formalization powering the parcel & 3PL up-cycle.
themes.driver: Freight/charter rates, terminalling tariffs and energy-cargo throughput.
